_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.context: All the free space left on the Pokémon Red and Green cartridge once the debug features were removed.

beats.text: Mew went in right at the very end.
beats.note: Programmer Shigeki Morimoto said the cartridge was really full and there wasn't room for much more on there.

beats.lead: It was not a secret plan
beats.text: It was left in for possible use after launch.
beats.note: Morimoto said it was kept in case it suited some post-launch activity.

beats.text: Mew turned up in some players' games.
beats.note: Morimoto: 'It looked like we planned all of this, but that wasn't the case.' Staff had been told not to tamper with a single bit after debugging ended.

beats.text: Over 78,000 people entered to win Mew.
beats.note: CoroCoro Comic's April 1996 Legendary Pokémon Offer had just 20 winners.

beats.name: Shigeki Morimoto
beats.role: Game Freak programmer who added Mew after the debug features were removed.

beats.line: 300 bytes became gaming's best known secret.
